answer: A spiral serializes registration: each identity extends the head by 2^20 sequential cipher iterations seeded by its public key and its signature, starting at the head the last segment left, so none can be parallelized or precomputed. Weight is capped by each ivory record, a signed chain adding one layer per epoch; splices break its links. One honest agent pays one segment, ten minutes; a farm with 1,000 identities queues behind 1,000 segments, about a week, whatever it rents, each starting near zero. Auditors replay segments from the prior head and reject forks, skips, and reused links.
